learning_outcomes.text: The student should have basic chemical knowledge associated with structure of matter, states of matter.
The student should have basic inorganic knowledge associated with the structure of metals, alloys, electron conductivity as well as basic organic knowledge associated with fuels and polymers
The student should have basic knowledge associated wit physicochemical characterization techniques of construction materials.

syllabus_topics: The structure of matter, elements, periodic table, compounds
Metals and alloys, solid state band theory.
Basic crystallography, unit cell, symmetry elements, crystallographic defect
Selected methods of solid materials characterizations
teaching_methods: traditional lecture with the use of transparencies and slides
self study - self studies and preparation for examination
assessment_rules: The final grade (P) is based on the forming grade (F1) obtained during the semester. F1 is evaluated by a test covering PEK_W01 - PEK_W03.
bibliography: Chemical Principles, Atkins Peter William, Jones Loretta, Palgrave Macmillan
Chemistry, Michell J. Sienlo and Robert A. Plane, both of Cornell University, Ithaca, New York.
degree: Mechanical Engineering and Machine Building (I level, full-time)
